<!--
TENTATIVE. Written 2026-08-04 to Luciano's design. Not numbered, not in the manuscript.

THE DESIGN. Every other figure in this set marginalises or crosses the three design variables. This
one holds two fixed and moves the third, out of a single corner:

    ORIGIN   N_ch = 10,  noise label = 0.1,  Delta*k_off = 0.01

and then three rays, one per axis. The corner is chosen so that the INTERVAL effect is negligible
there: at Delta*k_off = 0.01, and with p_open = 1/2 so the relaxation rate is twice k_off, the
averaging correction is of order 2 per cent. That is what makes the origin a VERIFICATION point.

WHY THE ORIGIN IS NOISE 0.1 AND NOT 0.05. At 0.05 the only member on disk is IR. NR, INR and R have
no cell there, so 0.05 cannot be a shared origin.

WHAT IT TESTS, and the prediction, stated so it can fail:

  (1) AT THE ORIGIN the two members of each pair must agree to within about 2 per cent, because at
      Delta*k_off = 0.01 there is almost nothing to average. INR -> NR and IR -> R is a LIMIT the
      code must satisfy, and it is a limit that does not come from the code under test. This is the
      cheapest exactness anchor available for the interval half of the implementation, and it needs
      no run. If the pair does not close at the origin, either the interval is not short enough,
      which shows as a gap that scales with Delta, or something is wrong.
  (2) ALONG N_ch both members of a pair should walk together toward 1 in the SAMPLE part (the
      per-sample Gaussian becomes exact) and SEPARATE in the CORRELATION part (which is what
      conditioning on the interval ends removes). That is the double dissociation, resolved by axis.
  (3) ALONG THE INTERVAL the pairs should open, and the opening is the interval axis measured.
  (4) ALONG NOISE both should return to 1, because instrumental noise buries the gating fluctuation.

THE ONE-AT-A-TIME LIMIT, stated because it bites here. Rays cannot see interactions, and there is a
known one: the R-to-IR gap on the k_off correlation grows from about 0.11 at N_ch = 10 to about 0.55
at N_ch = 10^4 (Figure 4-figure supplement 4). So the interval ray launched from N_ch = 10 shows the
SMALLEST separation this design can produce. The origin is the right place to verify coincidence and
the wrong place to demonstrate separation. The companion notebook figure_4_interval_pairs.Rmd runs
the interval axis from both ends of the channel axis for that reason.

TWO ANCHORS IN ONE FIGURE, and they must not be read as three views of one computation. The bias row
is on battery_sim_G at theta_sim, because at theta_pool the score vanishes by construction and the
bias is zero there by definition. The sample and correlation rows are on battery_pool_G at
theta_pool, which is where the information comparison is clean. The row strip says which.

THE BOOTSTRAP, verified against the code, because what it resamples decides what the bar means.

  IT IS THE CLASSICAL NONPARAMETRIC BOOTSTRAP, not the Poisson one. generate_bootstrap_indices
  (legacy/bootstrap.h:44) draws n indices uniformly with replacement at fixed resample size, and
  bootstrap_it pre-draws every replicate's indices serially so the result is seed-reproducible
  independently of the thread count. There is a Moment_poisson_bootstrap class in the tree; it is
  never instantiated anywhere and is dead code. Do not describe this as a Poisson bootstrap.

  IT RESAMPLES GROUPS, NOT RECORDINGS. src/core/likelihood.cpp:4278 says so in capitals, and :4622
  gives the reason: the per-group theta-hat are the iid units, and each resampled group is expanded
  to its recordings inside the computation. With group_size 100 over 10^4 recordings that is about a
  hundred units, and the same comment warns that few groups collapse the intervals. The width of the
  bar therefore depends in part on how the ensemble was grouped, which is a design decision and not
  a property of the estimator. B = 100 replicates, readable from the bootstrap_count column.

  THE CENTRE IS THE MEDIAN, quantile_level 0.5, and not the emitted mean. Every quantity here is a
  nonlinear functional of accumulated moments, a ratio of matrices or a product of eigenvalues, so
  the mean over replicates is not the statistic of the full ensemble: there is a Jensen bias, and
  this project has already measured one instance (the affine-invariant distance emitted as
  E_boot[d_AI] is biased up near the identity). For a positive right-skewed bootstrap distribution
  the mean sits above the median, which pushes a distortion away from 1 and would manufacture
  exactly the gap this figure exists to test.

  DO NOT TRANSFER THIS READING to the time-resolved diagnostics. Those go through
  bootstrap_it_two_to_Probit with two INDEPENDENT index sets and no pairing, and the header of
  bootstrap_it_two states that there the bootstrap is a comparison-of-estimators tool and not a
  re-recording-variance estimator. Different family, different meaning.

TRAP inherited from supplement 4: the delta dependence is NOT monotone and carries a kappa ~ 1e5
corner at Delta*k_off = 1, where the sample distortion deflates to about 0.44. The right-hand end of
the interval ray will misbehave and the caption has to own it rather than be surprised by it.

TRAP: the "noise" label is not the physical noise. current_noise = label/1000, and the dimensionless
noise is one tenth of the label. The axis here is the label, as everywhere else in this set.

ILSE is absent. The classical arm has no interval-aware sibling on disk yet, so the third pair
(LSE vs ILSE) is declared in PAIRS and will appear on the next knit once those cells exist.
-->

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
suppressMessages({ library(tidyverse) })
```

```{r constants}
DATA_DIRS <- c("../data/1c2ae6f", "../data/87889e6", "../data/0ffbda7", "../data/1f7138b")

# pair = (interval-naive, interval-aware). LSE/ILSE stays declared and will light up when it exists.
PAIRS <- tribble(
  ~pair,      ~naive,       ~aware,
  "LSE/ILSE", "macro_LSE",  "macro_ILSE",
  "NR/INR",   "macro_NR",   "macro_INR",
  "R/IR",     "macro_R",    "macro_IR"
)
PAIR_COL <- c("LSE/ILSE" = "#999999", "NR/INR" = "#D55E00", "R/IR" = "#0072B2")

ORIGIN <- list(nch = 10, noise = "0.1", interval = 0.01)

# NOTE: every strip label below is parsed as plotmath (label_parsed), so a literal space is a
# syntax error. Spaces are written as ~ and the labels must stay valid R expressions.
QTY <- tribble(
  ~qty,     ~component,                                            ~battery,           ~lab,                         ~diag,
  "bias",   "Probit_statistics_Gaussian_Distortion_Induced_Bias",  "battery_sim_G",    "bias~at~theta[sim]",         FALSE,
  "sample", "Probit_statistics_Gaussian_Sample_Distortion",        "battery_pool_G",   "sample~at~theta[pool]",      TRUE,
  "corr",   "Probit_statistics_Likelihood_Correlation_Distortion", "battery_pool_G",   "correlation~at~theta[pool]", TRUE
)
# diag: the two distortions are MATRICES and the figure wants their diagonal, so param_index must
# equal param_col. The bias is a VECTOR: its param_col is empty, the equality evaluates to NA, and
# filtering on it silently drops every bias row. That is why an earlier knit produced no bias PDF.

PARAMS  <- c(off = 1, Num_ch_mean = 5)          # the two carrier directions
PAR_LAB <- c(off = "k[off]", Num_ch_mean = "N[ch]")

findf <- function(nch, algo, z, kind) {
  f <- file.path(DATA_DIRS,
       sprintf("figure_3_G_nch_%d_nsim_10000_%s_noise_%s_%s.csv", nch, algo, z, kind))
  f <- f[file.exists(f)]
  if (!length(f)) NA_character_ else f[1]
}

# every (algo, nch, noise) cell present on disk, so the rays are built from what exists
CELLS <- expand_grid(algo = unique(c(PAIRS$naive, PAIRS$aware)),
                     nch  = c(5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 200, 500, 1000, 2000, 5000, 10000),
                     z    = c("0.05","0.1","0.2","0.5","1","10","100","1000","10000","100000","1000000")) %>%
  mutate(has = pmap_lgl(list(nch, algo, z), ~ !is.na(findf(..1, ..2, ..3, "battery_pool_G")))) %>%
  filter(has) %>% select(-has)
cat("cells on disk:", nrow(CELLS), "\n")
```

```{r reader}
read_qty <- function(nch, algo, z, qrow) {
  f <- findf(nch, algo, z, qrow$battery)
  if (is.na(f)) return(NULL)
  read.csv(f, skip = 1, stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%
    filter(component_path == qrow$component,
           if (qrow$diag) param_index == param_col else TRUE, param_index %in% PARAMS,
           statistic == "value",
           probit == "quantile", quantile_level %in% c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975)) %>%
    transmute(algo = algo, nch = nch, noise = z,
              interval = as.numeric(interval_in_tau),
              param = names(PARAMS)[match(param_index, PARAMS)],
              key = case_when(quantile_level == 0.5   ~ "mid",
                              quantile_level == 0.025 ~ "lo",
                              TRUE                    ~ "hi"),
              value)
}

# a ray is: hold two of the three fixed at the origin, sweep the third over what both members have
ray_cells <- function(axis, naive, aware) {
  a <- CELLS %>% filter(algo %in% c(naive, aware))
  if (axis == "nch")      a <- a %>% filter(z == ORIGIN$noise)
  if (axis == "noise")    a <- a %>% filter(nch == ORIGIN$nch)
  if (axis == "interval") a <- a %>% filter(nch == ORIGIN$nch, z == ORIGIN$noise)
  # keep only design points where BOTH members exist, so every comparison is like for like
  a %>% group_by(nch, z) %>% filter(n_distinct(algo) == 2) %>% ungroup()
}

dat <- pmap_dfr(PAIRS, function(pair, naive, aware) {
  pmap_dfr(QTY, function(qty, component, battery, lab, diag) {
    qrow <- list(component = component, battery = battery, diag = diag)
    map_dfr(c("nch", "interval", "noise"), function(axis) {
      cc <- ray_cells(axis, naive, aware)
      if (!nrow(cc)) return(NULL)
      pmap_dfr(cc, function(algo, nch, z) read_qty(nch, algo, z, qrow)) %>%
        { if (!nrow(.)) . else
            (if (axis == "interval") . else filter(., interval == ORIGIN$interval)) } %>%
        mutate(pair = pair, qty = qty, axis = axis,
               member = if_else(algo == naive, "interval-naive", "interval-aware"),
               x = case_when(axis == "nch" ~ nch,
                             axis == "noise" ~ as.numeric(noise),
                             TRUE ~ interval))
    })
  })
})
stopifnot(nrow(dat) > 0)

d <- dat %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = key, values_from = value) %>%
  mutate(qty  = factor(qty, levels = QTY$qty, labels = QTY$lab),
         axis = factor(axis, levels = c("nch", "interval", "noise"),
                       labels = c("N[ch]", "Delta %.% k[off]", "noise~label")),
         member = factor(member, levels = c("interval-naive", "interval-aware")))
cat("curve points:", nrow(d), " pairs:", paste(unique(as.character(d$pair)), collapse = " "), "\n")
```

```{r plot, fig.width = 7.0, fig.height = 7.6}
# ONE PAIR PER COLUMN, AND EACH PAIR ON ITS OWN Y SCALE. facet_grid cannot do the second part: its
# free scales are shared along a row, so putting the pairs in the columns of one grid forces
# NR/INR and R/IR onto a common axis and the smaller of the two collapses. Each pair is therefore its
# own plot, composed side by side with patchwork, which is what figure_4_supp_common.R already does.
#
# NO DASHED LINES. Both members are solid and separated by colour alone.
#
# SCALES follow figure_6B.Rmd, the format reference for the line figures here: raw values in the
# data, the transform done by scale_x_log10 and scale_y_log10 with explicit breaks.
#
# BIAS AND DISTORTION ARE SEPARATE FIGURES, and that is forced. A distortion is a ratio null at 1 and
# belongs on a log axis; a bias is already in log10 parameter units, is null at 0 and takes both
# signs, so it cannot share one.
suppressMessages(library(patchwork))
MEM_COL  <- c("interval-naive" = "#D55E00", "interval-aware" = "#0072B2")
DIST_BRK <- c(0.5, 0.7, 0.9, 1, 1.1, 1.3, 1.6, 2, 3, 5)
base_theme <- theme_bw(base_size = 8, base_family = "Helvetica") +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), panel.spacing = unit(.14, "cm"),
        strip.text = element_text(size = 7), strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0, size = 6.5),
        axis.text = element_text(size = 6), legend.position = "bottom",
        legend.key.size = unit(.6, "lines"), legend.text = element_text(size = 7.5),
        plot.title = element_text(size = 8, hjust = .5),
        plot.margin = margin(3, 4, 2, 3))

one_pair <- function(dd, pr, logy, ylab) {
  g <- ggplot(filter(dd, pair == pr), aes(x, mid, colour = member, fill = member)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = if (logy) 1 else 0, colour = "grey55", linewidth = .3) +
    geom_linerange(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), linewidth = .45, alpha = .8) +
    geom_line(linewidth = .5) + geom_point(size = .9) +
    scale_x_log10() +
    scale_colour_manual(values = MEM_COL) + scale_fill_manual(values = MEM_COL) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = ylab, colour = NULL, fill = NULL, title = pr) + base_theme
  if (logy) g <- g + scale_y_log10(breaks = DIST_BRK, labels = as.character(DIST_BRK))
  g
}

for (pp in names(PARAMS)) {
  for (blk in list(list(sel = QTY$lab[-1], logy = TRUE,  tag = "distortion",
                        ylab = "distortion (null = 1)", h = 7.2,
                        fac = facet_grid(axis + qty ~ ., scales = "free_y",
                                         labeller = label_parsed)),
                   list(sel = QTY$lab[1],  logy = FALSE, tag = "bias",
                        ylab = expression("bias  ("*log[10]~units*")"), h = 4.4,
                        fac = facet_grid(axis ~ ., scales = "free_y",
                                         labeller = label_parsed)))) {
    dd <- d %>% filter(param == pp, qty %in% blk$sel)
    prs <- unique(as.character(dd$pair))
    if (!length(prs)) next
    gl <- lapply(prs, function(pr)
      one_pair(dd, pr, blk$logy, if (pr == prs[1]) blk$ylab else NULL) + blk$fac)
    g <- wrap_plots(gl, nrow = 1) +
      plot_annotation(subtitle = parse(text = PAR_LAB[pp])) +
      plot_layout(guides = "collect") & theme(legend.position = "bottom")
    print(g)
    ggsave(sprintf("Figure_4_rays_%s_%s.pdf", blk$tag, pp), g,
           width = 3.1 * length(prs), height = blk$h)
  }
}
```

```{r origin-check}
# THE VERIFICATION NUMBER. At the origin each pair must close. Anything above a few per cent is the
# result, not a rounding issue.
cat("\n=== closure at the origin (N_ch", ORIGIN$nch, "noise", ORIGIN$noise,
    "Delta*k_off", ORIGIN$interval, ") ===\n")
d %>%
  filter(axis == "N[ch]", x == ORIGIN$nch) %>%
  select(pair, qty, param, member, mid) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = member, values_from = mid) %>%
  mutate(rel_gap = abs(`interval-aware` - `interval-naive`) /
                   pmax(abs(`interval-naive`), 1e-12)) %>%
  arrange(desc(rel_gap)) %>%
  print(n = 40)
```
